html:
An Iraqi poet and critic from Baghdad who was among the first to write free verse in Arabic, breaking with the fixed metres and single rhyme that had ruled Arabic poetry for some fifteen centuries.

She grew up in a family of writers; her mother was also a poet. In 1947 she wrote "Cholera", a poem about an epidemic in Egypt, in lines of uneven length built on a repeated metrical foot instead of the classical two-part line. In the same years Badr Shakir al-Sayyab was trying the same thing, and the two are usually named together as the founders of the new form.

She did not only write poems. Her book Issues in Contemporary Poetry (1962) set out the rules of the new verse and defended it, though she later worried it had gone too far. She studied in Baghdad and the United States, taught at universities in Iraq and Kuwait, and left Iraq in 1970. She spent her last years in Cairo, where she died in 2007.
sum: An Iraqi poet and critic from Baghdad who was among the first to write free verse in Arabic, breaking with the fixed metres and single rhyme that had ruled Arabic poetry for some fifteen centuries.
